skill.displayName: 睿观-图片政策合规监测

llm.summary: The skill does the advertised image compliance check, but it also includes under-scoped account, token, payment, upload, persistence, and silent feedback behaviors that users should review carefully.

dimensions.detail: Network use and API-key environment variables are expected for this service, but several sensitive endpoints are environment-overridable and can send API keys, SMS login data, bearer tokens, session metadata, or uploaded image data to the configured origin without an allowlist.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden installer, background worker, or automatic startup mechanism was found. The onboarding guide does suggest persisting the LinkFox API key in shell startup files, but that step is presented to the user.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions trigger the skill for broad image-to-violation matching, require uploading local images to obtain a public URL, invoke onboarding for auth/billing errors, and direct automatic feedback API reporting without interrupting the user; these flows need clearer user consent and scoping.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill intentionally writes full API responses, caches, session metadata, and payment QR artifacts locally; the implementation can fall back to home or temp directories despite documentation saying not to write to /tmp or to fail when the current directory is unavailable.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core Ruiguan image compliance API is coherent with the stated purpose, but the artifact also supports SMS login, API-key generation, account/package lookup, order creation, payment QR rendering, public local-image upload, and feedback reporting, which materially expand the skill beyond a narrow image checker.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending product image URLs or uploaded local images to LinkFox/Ruiguan, storing full responses locally, and using the bundled LinkFox account and billing helper. Avoid using it with private, signed, proprietary, or regulated images unless you accept public-link exposure and local retention. Review any onboarding or payment action before running it, and do not set endpoint override environment variables unless you fully trust the destination.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: Confirmed. Authenticated network calls are expected, but unrestricted environment-controlled base URLs for API-key, SMS, token, and payment requests are not sufficiently scoped for the sensitivity of the data sent.
[LP3] unexpected: Partly confirmed. Network, environment variables, and file writes are visible in the artifacts, but their full scope is not cleanly permissioned or minimized.
[TP4] unexpected: Confirmed as a Review concern. The account onboarding and billing capabilities are disclosed in references, but they are high-impact additions to a compliance-check skill and are not reflected in the frontmatter purpose.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed for onboarding. Phone registration, SMS login, API-token issuance, plan listing, and payment support are broader than the advertised image compliance function.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed for onboarding and billing. The user must choose phone, plan, and payment method, so this is not automatic theft or charging, but it still handles personal data and commerce inside an unexpectedly scoped skill.
[SDI-1] expected: Confirmed for result persistence, with caveats. Saving results is disclosed and can support the workflow, but persisting full responses and metadata by default is more exposure than necessary.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed. The script documentation says /tmp is forbidden and an unwritable current directory should error, while the implementation falls back to home and temp locations.
[SDI-1] expected: Downgraded for upload behavior. Uploading a local image is coherent because the API requires a public image URL, but it still creates a third-party data-transfer path that needs explicit user awareness.
[SDI-2] expected: Confirmed as a privacy concern. The upload script sets public-read and returns a public URL, which fits the public URL requirement but can expose sensitive product images.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Confirmed. The trigger text can activate the skill even without explicit compliance wording, which increases the chance of unintended paid calls or image transmission.
[SQP-2] expected: Confirmed. Sending an image URL to LinkFox/Ruiguan is central to the tool, but the instructions lack strong consent and data-minimization guidance for sensitive images or private URLs.
[SSD-3] expected: Confirmed. Full-response saving and optional full stdout output are documented, but they retain more user and detection data than the narrow task requires.
